style: Compares every passage plan detail with ECDIS, sailing directions, DNV and ALRS
Does manual calculations of pilotage legs with a calculator
Sits at the PC and checks the TEC-25 point by point

questions.q: How do you check parallel indexing and LDL inside safety contour?
What are the amendment procedures for the passage plan?
How do you check and maintain the echo sounder, and compare depth at berth?
What is the working principle of GPS?
What is the working principle of AIS and what is STDMA?
What tests are entered in the GMDSS log book?
What is the difference between S band and X band radar?
Why is a solid state radar different from a magnetron radar and what maintenance is needed?
What is the working principle of SART and how does it appear on radar?
What is the distance and working duration of the Aldis lamp, and where are spare bulbs?
What is the error log book and the definition of deviation and variation?
What is the working principle of a sextant and which angle is object altitude?
Which NAVWARNINGS and NAVTEX are applicable for the voyage?
How do you check the pilot card and master pilot exchange?
What is WGS84 and why are other datums not used in ECDIS?
What are the ECDIS IHO standards, Chart 1 and date dependent features?
What is VECS mode and gas calibration?
What action do you take if cargo goes into a crew member's eyes?

checks.item: Passage plan details compared with ECDIS, sailing directions, DNV and ALRS
Parallel indexing and LDL inside safety contour
TEC-25 checked point by point on PC
Echo sounder checks, maintenance and depth comparison at berth
AIS tests entered in GMDSS log book
Pilot card and master pilot exchange
ECDIS IHO standards, Chart 1 and date dependent feature

tips: Be ready to do manual pilotage leg calculations with a calculator
Know the working principles of GPS, AIS, SART, sextant and radar types
Expect point by point checks of the TEC-25 on the PC
summary: A 2.5 hour SIRE 2.0 inspection on the bridge at Kawasaki, Japan, by inspector I Hag Sebo. He was very detailed on passage planning, ECDIS and bridge equipment, doing manual calculations and checking the TEC-25 point by point. The bridge was clear with no observations and he gave two good observations; he is quite old and wants answers quickly.
